Header: 2026-06-11 14:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Kapoor, Jordan Lee (Redwood) — Maya Ruiz, Tom Becker, Liam OConnor (NexaHealth)

Summary: quick status sync - onboarding checklist, infra access, staging readiness, and benchmark planning.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Alex from Redwood, i'll kick off, quick agenda is status, blockers, then bench schedule. Priya, you wanna do quick infra readout?
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: yeah sure, thanks. So from our side we did the initial model load on staging yesterday. There was one hiccup with the quantized checkpoint, um Red wood Dedicated — oh sorry — Redwood Dedicated variant had a small mapping mismatch so i re-ran the conversion, should be fine.
[00:35] Tom Becker: ok, that matches what i saw. i tried to spin up the staging runner and the KV cache wasn't persisted across the node restart, looks like a mount permission thing.
[00:50] Priya Kapoor: right, likely the nfs mount on the k8s node, we saw similar before. For the POC we recommended ephemeral cache for bench runs but persisting for longer runs helps latency.
[01:05] Maya Ruiz: quick q, can you remind us — for the benchmark we agreed 95th percentile latency target of 350ms for our chat flows? is that still realistic on the hosted tier or do we need Dedicated?
[01:20] Priya Kapoor: good question. For the seq lengths you're sending in the sample prompts, hosted should hit around 300–400ms p95 with batching disabled; if you want <300ms consistently, Dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernels is safer. There's a cost tradeoff though.
[01:40] Liam OConnor: yeah cost's a big factor — we have a constrained budget for Q3. we need an estimate on the delta between hosted and Dedicated.
[01:50] Alex Chen: i'll send a short pricing delta tonight, incl the cost per 1M tokens and expected throughput.
[02:00] Maya Ruiz: also on security, we need to confirm KMS and data residency. we can't ship PHI outside region eu-west-1, so the private deployment option or regional hosting is important.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: noted — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and regional control plane; we have a SOC 2 report and can share KMS integration notes. we'll include the docs.
[02:30] Tom Becker: right, but practically we need VPC peering for staging to access our internal data store. we raised a ticket for peering and provided account ids. any blockers from your side?
[02:45] Priya Kapoor: we just need the service account and a couple subnets; once peering is set we can verify the egress rules. For now we can run the smoke tests with limited data.
[03:00] Alex Chen: sounds good. action items — Priya will run smoke tests, Tom will grant service account + peering, Maya will send production prompts.
[03:10] Maya Ruiz: one more thing — audit logs, do you provide token-level tracing? our compliance team wants per-request traces and retention for 90 days.
[03:25] Jordan Lee: yes we have token-level cost & latency breakdowns and audit logs that integrate with your SIEM; retention is configurable — we can propose 90 days in the security packet.
[03:40] Tom Becker: ok great. For the bench run itself, when do you want to execute? we have a maintenance window wed morning.
[03:50] Priya Kapoor: wed morning 10–12 PST works for our infra team, how about 6/15 10:00–12:00 PST?
[03:58] Maya Ruiz: that works for us. please confirm run-of-show and the test harness list.
[04:05] Priya Kapoor: will do — we'll share the benchmark spreadsheet with exact prompts, concurrency, and metrics (p50, p95, cost per 1k tokens).
[04:20] Alex Chen: competitor note — Maya asked earlier if we compared to Anthropic and AWS Bedrock. we ran a brief perf sweep internally; we'll share high-level notes but the best is to run a side-by-side in your env.
[04:35] Liam OConnor: agreed, can we include OpenAI as well in the sweep?
[04:40] Priya Kapoor: yes we can, but note licensing for some endpoints may require accounts on your side.
[04:48] Maya Ruiz: ok. small nit — earlier you mentioned KV cache persistence, can that be toggled per-request? sometimes we want cold-start sim.
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: yes. our runtime supports prefix/KV caching toggles and we can simulate cold-starts by clearing the cache between runs. we'll add that to the bench plan.
[05:10] Tom Becker: on infra details, i have one conf — the peering request used the wrong account id in the ticket, i'll correct it and resend by EOD.
[05:20] Alex Chen: perfect. i will send the security packet (SOC2 summary, SAML SSO instructions, KMS integration notes) and the pricing delta tonight.
[05:30] Maya Ruiz: thanks. anything else?
[05:35] Jordan Lee: nothing from me.
[05:38] Alex Chen: recap — actions: Priya run smoke tests (due 6/13), Tom fix peering + grant service account (due 6/14), Alex send security + pricing (due 6/12), Maya to share prompts (due 6/13), benchmark scheduled 2026-06-15 10–12 PST. We'll share bench spreadsheet and test harness. Thanks everyone.
[05:58] Maya Ruiz: thanks, bye.
